children: Bernstein has a reassuring message for Howmet Aerospace
investors after SpaceX's plans to make some turbine components triggered a sharp selloff in the stock.

Howmet shares dropped as much as 9% Monday after SpaceX said it intends to produce turbine blades and vanes for a 20-gigawatt power project serving AI data centers in Bastrop, Texas. Bernstein analyst Douglas Harned said the move may reflect tight industry capacity rather than a threat to Howmet's core business.

The firm points to a supply shortage in the industrial gas turbine market, where demand has been rising faster than available manufacturing capacity. Howmet has already started expanding output, with six more projects expected by the end of the fourth quarter that could raise turbine-blade capacity by as much as 38% from the first quarter of 2025.
Bernstein also noted that Howmet's customer agreements extend through 2030. It maintained an Outperform rating and raised its price target to $328 from $248.
Bernstein's response suggests SpaceX's move may have been overinterpreted by investors, leaving the focus on how long AI-related power demand keeps turbine suppliers busy.

title: SpaceX Sends Howmet Stock Tumbling -- Bernstein Sees a Buying Opportunity
